description: Portable conformance fixtures for the Axiom Server IR. Each entry is a self-contained JSON document: the Server IR, the state to start from, the principals, the invocations to perform and the results required. Running them needs no part of this implementation.

fixtures.name: mutation-commits
fixtures.description: An action within its guards commits every write, and derived state follows.

fixtures.name: guard-refuses
fixtures.description: A guard that does not hold refuses the invocation, naming its failure mode.

fixtures.name: constraint-rolls-back
fixtures.description: Iteration N sees the writes of iterations before it, so two lines for one part are counted together — and the invariant then rolls the whole action back.

fixtures.name: for-each-provisional
fixtures.description: The same two-line shape, within stock: 10 − 4 − 4, not 10 − 4 twice.

fixtures.name: transition-constraint
fixtures.description: A rule about how state may change refuses a raise, and permits a fall.

fixtures.name: authorization
fixtures.description: Authorization is evaluated on the authority, with the caller bound to PRINCIPAL.

fixtures.name: argument-validation
fixtures.description: Untrusted arguments are checked against declared parameter types.

fixtures.name: idempotent-retry
fixtures.description: A repeated request id is answered from the record, not executed again.

fixtures.name: concurrent-invocations
fixtures.description: Three callers each want four of a stock of five. Exactly one may commit; the rest are refused by the guard against authoritative state.

fixtures.name: restart
fixtures.description: Committed state is restored exactly on restart, and a rolled-back write never reappears.

fixtures.name: integration-query-success
fixtures.description: A successful integration query binds its result and commits.

fixtures.name: integration-query-timeout
fixtures.description: A non-cooperating adapter cannot wedge the invocation past its declared timeoutMs; the runtime enforces the deadline itself.

fixtures.name: timed-trigger-polling
fixtures.description: An interval trigger fires the query and writes its result, with no real wait.

fixtures.name: effect-success-event
fixtures.description: A succeeded effect dispatches its structured outcome to a system-only follow-up action — never reachable by a client directly.

fixtures.name: system-only-action-rejects-client
fixtures.description: An anonymous client cannot directly invoke an action reachable only by a trigger, event or effect outcome.
